title: Faire faire : organiser plutôt qu'exécuter
summary: Express arranging or causing an action, distinguish the performer from the affected object, and keep `fait` invariable before an infinitive.
objectives: Use `faire` + infinitive to distinguish arranging from personally doing.
Express who performs the action and what is affected.
Place pronouns and keep causative `fait` invariable.

sections.title: The subject causes or arranges the action
paragraphs: A causative construction presents someone as arranging, causing or having an action done, rather than necessarily performing it personally. French uses conjugated `faire` + infinitive. Compare `je répare le vélo` (I repair it myself) and `je fais réparer le vélo` (I have it repaired). The context determines whether there is payment, instruction, permission or simple causation; `faire` does not by itself mean force.

Conjugate only `faire`: `je fais réparer, tu fais réparer, il/elle/on fait réparer, nous faisons réparer, vous faites réparer, ils/elles font réparer`. In other tenses: `je faisais réparer, j'ai fait réparer, je ferai réparer, je voudrais faire réparer`. Keep the performed action in the infinitive.

The performer (agent) is who carries out the infinitive's action; the affected object is what that action concerns. With no other direct object, the performer can be a direct complement: `faire venir un technicien`. With an affected object too, identify the performer with `à` or `par`: `faire relire le texte à/par une collègue`. `Par` often makes agency clearer; both can be legitimate.

examples.english: We are having an interpreter come.

examples.french: La responsable **fait relire** le contrat **par** un juriste.
examples.english: The manager has a legal specialist reread the contract.
examples.note: The contract is affected; the legal specialist is the performer.

examples.french: Le professeur **fait lire** le dialogue **aux** élèves.
examples.english: The teacher has the pupils read the dialogue.
examples.note: An object and a performer are both expressed.

mistakes.why: The second verb must remain an infinitive.

sections.title: Pronouns precede the `faire` group
paragraphs: Treat `faire` + infinitive as a tight causative group. Object pronouns normally go before the conjugated `faire`, or before its auxiliary in a compound tense: `je le fais réparer`, `je l'ai fait réparer`. If `faire` itself follows another verb, they can stand before `faire`: `je vais le faire réparer`.

A person made to act can be `le/la/les` when no other direct object is present: `je la fais venir`. With a separate direct object, a pronominal performer often becomes `lui/leur`: `je lui fais lire le texte`; `je le lui fais lire`. Do not assume every 'her' is `la`: choose from the construction.

In `se faire` + infinitive, the subject is involved as an affected or benefiting person: `se faire couper les cheveux`. This may describe an arranged service, but the construction does not always imply willingness; `se faire voler son vélo` describes an unwanted theft. Read the situation.

examples.french: Cette imprimante, je **la fais nettoyer** régulièrement.
examples.english: I have this printer cleaned regularly.

examples.french: Le résumé ? Je **le lui fais lire** avant la réunion.
examples.english: The summary? I have him/her read it before the meeting.
examples.note: `Le` is the text; `lui` is the performer.

sections.title: `Fait` + infinitive is invariable
paragraphs: In the causative, `fait` immediately followed by an infinitive never agrees, even with a preceding feminine/plural object or a reflexive subject: `les affiches que j'ai fait imprimer`; `elles se sont fait aider`. This exception concerns `fait` + infinitive, not ordinary `faire` on its own: `les affiches que j'ai faites` means the posters I made myself.

Affirmative imperative pronouns follow `faire` with hyphens: `fais-le réparer`. Negative commands restore pre-verbal placement: `ne le fais pas réparer`. Do not attach the object after the infinitive as though this were an ordinary affirmative imperative of `réparer`.

examples.french: Les affiches que nous avons **fait imprimer** sont prêtes.
examples.english: The posters we had printed are ready.

examples.french: Les affiches que nous avons **faites** sont originales.
examples.english: The posters we made are original.
examples.note: Without an infinitive, ordinary preceding-object agreement applies.

examples.english: This socket is damaged. Have it replaced.
examples.note: Affirmative imperative of `faire` with the object pronoun after it.

mistakes.avoid: Les portes que j'ai faites réparer sont solides.
mistakes.prefer: Les portes que j'ai fait réparer sont solides.
mistakes.why: Causative `fait` before an infinitive is always invariable.

practice.prompt: Express that you arrange, rather than personally perform, a repair. Supply faire in the present + réparer: Je ___ la porte.
practice.explanation: Faire is conjugated; réparer remains infinitive.

practice.prompt: In Elle fait traduire le rapport par Samir, who translates?
Replace le moteur: Je fais vérifier le moteur. Supply the entire verb group after Je.
Supply only faire's participle: Les fenêtres que j'ai ___ nettoyer sont ouvertes.
practice.explanation: Fait before an infinitive is invariable.

practice.prompt: Supply faire in the present + venir: Nous ___ un plombier.
practice.explanation: Nous faisons plus the infinitive venir.

practice.prompt: Supply the performer preposition: Je fais vérifier les comptes ___ une comptable. Accept either standard agent introduction.
practice.explanation: Both par and à can introduce the performer with a separate object; par makes agency especially explicit.

practice.prompt: Replace à Léa with a pronoun: Je fais lire le texte à Léa. Supply only the pronoun before fais.
practice.explanation: The text is already the direct object; the performer is indirect.

practice.prompt: Replace le texte and à Léa: Je fais lire le texte à Léa. Supply only the pronoun group before fais.
practice.explanation: Direct le followed by indirect performer lui.

practice.prompt: Replace la technicienne: Je fais venir la technicienne. Supply only the pronoun before fais.
practice.explanation: No other direct object: the performer is direct.

practice.prompt: Supply only faire's participle: Elles se sont ___ photographier.
practice.explanation: Reflexive causative fait is still invariable.

practice.prompt: Use the affirmative tu imperative of faire with le and réparer. Supply only the complete verb group.
practice.explanation: The pronoun attaches after imperative fais.

practice.prompt: Does Il s'est fait voler son vélo imply he wanted the theft?
choices: No; se faire can describe an unwanted event affecting him.
Yes; all se faire constructions express consent.
answers: No; se faire can describe an unwanted event affecting him.
practice.explanation: Causative-like form does not always imply intentional arrangement.

practice.prompt: Make Fais-le imprimer negative with ne...pas. Supply the complete verb group.
Supply only faire's participle without a following infinitive: Les maquettes que j'ai ___ sont ici.
practice.explanation: Ordinary faire agrees with preceding feminine plural que.

practice.prompt: Replace la voiture and keep the future plan: Je vais faire réparer la voiture. Supply only the group after vais.
practice.explanation: The pronoun stands before infinitive faire.

practice.prompt: Supply faire in passé composé + contrôler: Nous ___ l'installation.
practice.explanation: Only faire becomes a compound finite form; contrôler stays infinitive.

production_task.prompt: Write to a building committee about work you arranged, not performed yourself. Name one professional, replace one object with a pronoun and distinguish one thing you did personally.
production_task.model_answer: J'ai fait vérifier le chauffage par une technicienne. La serrure était usée : je l'ai fait remplacer. Les affiches, en revanche, je les ai faites moi-même.
production_task.translation: I had a technician check the heating. The lock was worn: I had it replaced. The posters, however, I made myself.
rubric: Ordinary `faites` agrees with the preceding feminine plural object.
